subject: Evaluation roadmap & acceptance test plan for LuminaHealth pilot
messages:
From: Sara O'Neil <sara.oneil@luminahealth.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot evaluation — defining success & next steps

Thanks Marcus — great demo today. Procurement looped me in to start formalizing the evaluation plan so we can get internal approvals. High level ask: we need a short mutual action plan that defines success criteria, concrete acceptance tests we can run against a 4‑week pilot, and clear exit gates before we commit to a full rollout.

What would help on our side: a) a mapped set of acceptance tests (functional + perf + security), b) target thresholds (latency, throughput, concordance), c) evidence artifacts we should collect, and d) a recommended timeline to move from pilot -> commit.

I attached a short template our PM uses (see: Lumina-eval-template.xlsx). Also flagging that SOC 2 evidence and a data retention statement will be required for our Security review. Can you own drafting the MAP and a test matrix?

Sara
Sara O'Neil
Head of ML Platforms, LuminaHealth
LuminaHealth | sara.oneil@luminahealth.com

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sara O'Neil <sara.oneil@luminahealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot evaluation — defining success & next steps

Sara — thanks for the note and the template, appreciated. We reviewed internally and sketched a two‑page MAP and a draft acceptance-test matrix. Goal is to keep the pilot scoped to 4 weeks with three decision checkpoints: week 1 (smoke + connectivity), week 3 (quality/perf), week 4 (go/no‑go evidence).

Draft outline I can share this week:
- Success criteria (business + technical): 1) Business acceptance: average task completion concordance >= 88% on Lumina sample set; 2) Latency: p95 generation < 600ms for 256 tokens; 3) Cost: projected token cost delta < 20% vs your benchmark.
- Exit gates: required pass on security checklist, no critical data leakage findings, sustained perf across 3 days.
- Acceptance tests: 1) Functional: 200 representative prompts (held‑out), concordance scoring + manual spot check, 2) Perf: load to expected QPS with 95th percentile latency check, 3) Safety: prompt injection probes and data egress checks.
- Evidence: test matrix (CSV), request/response logs (redacted), KV/prefix caching behavior notes, SOC2 evidence stub.

I attached our MAP draft (MAP-Lumina-v1.xlsx) and the acceptance‑test catalog (acceptance-test-matrix.pdf). Karthik, can you confirm the perf thresholds and owners? Lauren — could you loop in Security contact for SOC2/data retention?

Next step: propose a pilot start of Mon 9/20 so we can run the four weeks and present to your stakeholders the week of 10/18. Open to adjust.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: MAP-Lumina-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet stub); acceptance-test-matrix.pdf (doc stub)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Acceptance test owners & thresholds (draft)

Internal note — threading into the MAP draft. Proposed mapping of tests to owners and concrete thresholds: 
- Functional/concordance (owner: Karthik): 200 held‑out queries, automated concordance scoring >= 88% and manual review pass rate >= 92% across 30 samples. Evidence artifacts: scoring CSV, 30 manual review notes.
- Performance (owner: Marcus): target p50 < 180ms, p95 < 600ms at nominal pilot load (10 QPS sustained, burst to 30 QPS). Failure mode: p95 > 900ms or error rate > 1% for > 1 hour triggers rollback.
- Cost (owner: Lauren): projected token spend < $X per 100k tokens (X to finalise after their benchmark). Acceptance if projected monthly delta < 20% vs baseline.
- Security/compliance (owner: Security team, to be assigned): no high/critical findings for data handling; SOC2 evidence present.

I've attached a compact test checklist (acceptance-test-matrix.pdf) — when Marcus posts the MAP to Lumina Drive, I will export the perf harness and share runbook.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Attachments: acceptance-test-matrix.pdf (doc stub)

- Security: can you provide a named Security contact and a short data retention statement (we need to confirm retention window for logs and PII handling).
- Test data: we will provide a 1k prompt sample (de‑identified). Please confirm how you'll ingest it and whether we need a separate S3 bucket or can share via our secure Drive folder.

If we can get those items by Tue 9/15, Procurement will aim to sign the pilot SOW quickly. We're still targeting a kick on 9/20 pending the SOW.

-Sara

Sara — quick update and straight answers so Procurement can move: 
1) Security contact & retention: Lauren Bishop (lauren_bishop@redwood.ai) is owning Security coordination; short retention statement: "Request/response logs for the pilot will be retained for 30 days by default; redaction rules will be applied to remove PII per Lumina guidance; long‑term retention options available under Private deployment contract." I attached a SOC2 evidence stub for Security to review.

2) Ingest: we prefer a secure S3 bucket (we can provide a one‑time presigned URL) — if you want to use Drive we can accept that but S3 is easier for reproducible perf runs.

3) Acceptance blurb for SOW (one paragraph you can paste): 
"Pilot acceptance is defined as successful completion of the mutually‑agreed evaluation plan: the model must meet functional concordance >= 88% on the agreed held‑out sample, demonstrate p95 inference latency < 600ms under nominal pilot load, and present no unresolved security findings classified as high or critical. Evidence will be provided as a test matrix, request/response logs (redacted), and a summary report. Passing these checks permits LuminaHealth to proceed to a production rollout evaluation."

4) Timeline: deliver final MAP + test matrix by 9/15; SOW sign target 9/17; pilot start 9/20; week 1 smoke, week 3 quality report, week 4 go/no‑go presentation 10/18.

I've uploaded the MAP draft and acceptance matrix to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1LuminaPilotSpecs. Please confirm you received the sample prompts and whether S3 or Drive works.

If Procurement needs a slightly different blurb, let us know and we'll adapt.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this running.

—Marcus Lin
